content.comment_body: Is it possible to change the digital input of a [product_name] [version_no] using [product_name] [version_no] and an SMS command, or is it only possible to modify the digital transistor input/output of the [product_name] [version_no]? We connected the [product_name] to the [product_name] for monitoring outputs, and currently control the output via the [product_name] [version_no].

You can control both digital outputs of the [product_name] [version_no] via SMS and then connect up to two digital inputs of the [product_name]. Alternatively, sending an SMS can toggle a bit in the VM area, which can be used as a network input in the [product_name], allowing for more flexibility beyond just two inputs.

Currently, we use the first method, but we want the output of the [product_name] to automatically switch to 0 after two seconds. So, we intend to use the [product_name] instead of a relay as we currently do. What kind of SMS commands can set the network inputs of the [product_name] to 0 or 1? We now monitor the outputs of the [product_name] via SMS. Is the process similar for network inputs, only reversed?

If you want to switch a network input in the [product_name] via SMS, note that the [product_name] will set the input statically. This generally requires sending two SMS messages: one to turn on, and another to turn off. For example, 'Password; [product_name]=VM100,1,BYTE' to switch on, and 'Password; [product_name]=VM100,0,BYTE' to switch off. These commands toggle the VM bit V100.0. You can select other VM addresses depending on your setup. Dynamically switching network inputs (for a timed action) in the [product_name] requires an additional step in your program. I've attached a small example program to demonstrate both approaches.
Understood. Thank you very much; your explanation was much clearer than anything I found in the manual. This will help us move forward.
We programmed the [product_name], but each time we try to set the network input to 1, we get the message: '[product_name]=VM50,1,BYTE:No Success'. Any idea what might be causing this issue?
Have you declared the variable in the [product_name] [version_no]?

Please check [url]. It describes how to set up everything needed to perform an action with an SMS in the [product_name], including communication between two [product_name] Controllers via [product_name] [version_no] and SMS.
Everything is working perfectly now as intended. Thanks for the help!

analysis.insight_summary: Users requested guidance on how to remotely control network inputs of a [product_name] module using SMS via [product_name] communication modules. There was initial confusion regarding how static and dynamic input switching works through SMS, the need for multiple messages to toggle inputs, and a lack of clear documentation. Through forum advice, the users received explicit command formatting guidance and learned about necessary variable declarations, successfully resolving their problem.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek a simple and reliable way to remotely and dynamically operate network inputs of [product_name] modules with SMS, ideally with just one message, and expect clear, comprehensive documentation outlining the steps needed.
